title: Thunder Substack (by Andreea Popa): Thunder 2025, moving toward what matters before certainty arrives
summary: Andreea Popa's year-end reflection argues that 2025 was the year Thunder stopped waiting to feel ready and simply began: launching The Thunder Way event, writing the leadership book, and choosing collaboration over competition. It reports Cris Pop speaking at the New York and Cluj events and guiding Thunder Talks conversations, and describes the Thunderometer, a shared values check-in.

principles.text: Momentum comes from showing up fully and trusting your people, not from having everything figured out.
principles.quote: That momentum comes not from having everything figured out, but from showing up fully, believing in what you’re creating, and trusting that the people around you will meet you there.

principles.text: Lead yourself: own quality beyond your tasks, hold standards high, and build with intention.
principles.quote: Lead yourself through the work. Take ownership beyond your tasks, hold your standards high, and build with intention.

principles.text: Treat other companies as collaborators, not competitors, and contribute to a community together.
principles.quote: We’ve never bought into the idea of competition. To us, it’s always been about coming together and contributing to a community worth being part of, side by side.

principles.text: Build community in person: be present where people are and gather them around the same table.
principles.quote: Show up where people are. Pull chairs to the same table, invest in gathering together, and build community the timeless way, close by, present, and reminding one another we’re in this together.

principles.text: Leadership is about being fully human and present, not about titles or authority.
principles.quote: From the truth that leadership is not about titles, nor about authority. It will always come back to showing up, fully human, fully present, and leading from that place of authenticity.

principles.text: Use shared principles as a compass to notice drift, not as rules that dictate what to do.
principles.quote: It doesn’t tell us what to do, but it helps us sense when we’re moving in the right direction.
